Nina (Partnerships): Hey team — vendor call recap attached. We need to lock down cost inputs from HW partners for our marketplace pricing model. Key asks: reserved instance tiers, spot/interruptible pricing windows, supply SLAs, and any marketplace commissions.

Ravi (Finance): Can you paste the exact fields we need? I'll template the model.

Nina (Partnerships): Sure — short list: `sku`, `gpu_type`, `region`, `on_demand_hourly`, `reserved_hourly_1yr`, `reserved_hourly_3yr`, `reserved_min_commit` (vCPU/GPU hours), `spot_hourly`, `spot_interruption_rate_pct`, `max_burst_capacity`, `availability_pct`, `marketplace_fee_pct`, `contract_notice_days`.

Sam (Infra Ops): For infra planning we also need per-sku memory, nvlink topology, and preemption granularity (per-instance vs per-pod). Add `cold_start_penalty_ms` if applicable.

Yvonne (Sales): On commercial side, ask partners for EDP/committed discount ladders and any channel/co-sell rebates. Also capture exclusivity windows for joint announcements.

Nina (Partnerships): Agreed. I pinged the partner product lead and asked for a CSV with those columns. They said: "can deliver reserved/spot pricing + a monthly supply forecast for next 12 months." They were vague on interruption rate.

Ravi (Finance): Important: we model spot with an expected interruption hazard rate and couple that with fallback cost to our fallback model (e.g., smaller cheaper GPU). Provide formula we will use: `expected_spot_cost = spot_price + interruption_rate * (fallback_cost + migration_overhead)`. We'll need partner's estimated `interruption_rate` per region/sku.

Sam (Infra Ops): Also request `reservation_allocation_window` (start/end dates) and whether partners can carve dedicated pools for Redwood Dedicated customers. That affects committed capacity planning.

Nina (Partnerships): Noted. Partner asked whether we want committed capacity as "reserved instances" (time-bound discounted skus) vs "capacity reservations" (guaranteed nodes). We should specify both.

Yvonne (Sales): For marketplace listing we need `billing_unit` (hour/minute/token), `minimum_purchase`, and whether partner supports invoice-based settlement vs marketplace billing.

cloud-partner-bot: Reminder: partnership-doc-template.csv available at https://internal.redwood/partnerships/templates/partner-cost-template.csv

Ravi (Finance): Quick sanity check — ask partners for any volume tiers (e.g., >10k GPU-hours/month -> additional 10% off) and blackout dates (holiday supply constraints). We'll bake tiers into our pricing engine.

Nina (Partnerships): I've drafted an email with an attached CSV schema and modeling notes. Will share here before sending. Quick preview: 
```
sku,gpu_type,region,on_demand_hourly,reserved_hourly_1yr,reserved_hourly_3yr,reserved_min_commit,spot_hourly,spot_interruption_rate_pct,max_burst_capacity,availability_pct,marketplace_fee_pct,contract_notice_days,reservation_allocation_window_start,reservation_allocation_window_end,volume_tiers
```
Sam (Infra Ops): One more ops note: ask for historical utilization % by SKU (last 6 months) and any I/O or thermal throttling events. That will influence achievable utilization in our batching models.

Yvonne (Sales): Also capture PR/announce constraints: embargo date, partner-approved messaging, joint quote templates. We'll coordinate product/marketing.

Nina (Partnerships): OK I'll send the CSV + modeling notes in an hour. Ravi/Sam/Yvonne — please add any final fields now. If we get the partner file this week we can run baseline TCO scenarios for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Ravi (Finance): Add `early_termination_fee` and `price_escalation_pct_per_year` to model assumptions.

Sam (Infra Ops): Add `preemption_grace_seconds` and `mttr_for_preemption` as placeholders.

Yvonne (Sales): Add `co_selling_enabled` (bool) and `preferred_partner_contact` fields.

Nina (Partnerships): Great. I'll update schema and send. Thanks! :thumbsup:

cloud-partner-bot: Logged action: "partner_cost_request_sent" by Nina at 1751234600
